newsitem.title: UK: Jordan central bank hails increase in reserves.
newsitem.headline: Jordan central bank hails increase in reserves.

text.p: Rising foreign exchange reserves in Jordan show growing confidence in a country well on the way to structural reforms and economic stabilisation, the deputy-head of the Central Bank of Jordan Michele Marto said on Thursday.

Speaking at an investment conference in London organised by Swiss bank UBS Ltd, Marto said official reserves have risen by $200 million this year alone from $700 million at the end of last year and $427 million at the end of 1996.
"The vulnerability of the Jordanian economy to adverse external developments is gradually declining," said Marto.
The deputy-central bank chief said the target for official reserves this year is $1.06 billion. "I am sure it will be surpassed."

Reserve levels, which have been depeleted heavily in recent years by peristsnt speculative attacks on the dinar, were equivalent to 2.1 months of the country's imports at the end of 1996 and should be above 3.5-months worth this year, he said.
"Monetary policy will continue to be geared to strengthening confidence in the Jordan dinar," said Marto.
The politically-independent central bank's exchange rate policy targets the U.S. dollar, currently at 0.7080 dinar, and the currency is almost completely convertible.

Marto said current account transactions are not subject to any exchange controls and for the vast majority of foreign investors with assets in Jordan there is no restrictions on removing capital from the country.
"The cental bank believes the present exchange rate of the dinar reflects the fundamentals of the economy. The external imbalances have narrowed down," he said.

The central banker said the main objectives for 1997 are attaining gross domestic product growth of 6.5 pct, containing inflation to below 4 pct and lowering further the currency's vulnerability to external shocks.
"These are ambitious goals and we can assure you now that they will be realized by the end of the year."
